title: Liquidity Decisions Under Aggregate Constraints

data_provenance.text: The source contains locally authored aggregate OHLC, volume, spread, volatility, and print constraints; it is not real-market data.
Every displayed order, queue position, cancellation, and exchange event in the lesson is generated synthetic reconstruction.

historical_context.text: The aggregate fixture describes directional flow with a brief retracement over a thirty-second teaching window.
A bounded deterministic seed search selects one generated path that approximates the supplied aggregate constraints.

learning_objectives: Judge spread crossing while treating reconstructed queues as scenarios rather than observations.
Compare generated outcomes with disclosed aggregate targets and residuals.
Identify which apparent Level 2 facts are unavailable from the source.

event.text: A pedagogical aggregate constraint set described upward net movement with an intervening retracement.

market_context.text: The visible ladder was one deterministic synthetic path fitted to aggregate targets, not a recovered historical order book.

what_happened_next.text: Generated order flow depleted and replenished queues until the selected path reached its disclosed synthetic ending state.

why_session_matters.text: It trains execution decisions under a plausible constrained scenario while preserving the refusal to invent missing historical queues.

known_limitations: Historical Level 2 is missing; all displayed queues and order events are synthetic reconstruction.
The aggregate constraints are locally authored pedagogical inputs, not measured observations from a real instrument.
Constraint fitting does not make the selected order path historically true.
training_questions: Did displayed liquidity disappear before the move?
Was crossing the spread justified within this scenario?
Which conclusions would require historical Level 2 that the source does not provide?
